analysis.title: Cross Asset Outlook / FOMC Minutes / Carbonomics / Oil Services / ASML / Airtel / Europe Hardware / Tencent (19 Nov 2026)
key_insights: GS stays modestly pro-risk but favours more balance across and within assets as nominal and earnings growth approach a peak after the AI capex boom and the energy-driven inflation boost of 2026. Near-term risks are AI concerns, renewed energy shocks, more aggressive Fed tightening and fiscal concerns.

GS expects the balance between slowing growth and rates relief to drive risk appetite in 2027. A peak in nominal growth need not end the bull market if inflation falls and real growth holds. Easing energy prices and normalising inflation should limit further tightening and let bond yields decline gradually.

October FOMC minutes: 'most' participants supported holding the fed funds rate at 3.75-4.00%, and 'many' cited the benefits of accumulating additional information. 'A few' called the decision 'a close call'.
'Some' participants, including dissenters Governor Cook and President Hammack, favoured a 25bp hike and called the stance 'not sufficiently restrictive'.

'Almost all' FOMC participants judged that further action to raise the target range 'would likely be appropriate' under their baseline outlooks. 'A couple' said a hike larger than 25bp could warrant consideration at the next meeting if incoming inflation data are 'unfavorable'.

Carbonomics: de-carbonization is insufficient to limit warming to 1.5-2°C. The current trajectory is more likely to reach 2.5-2.9°C, and coal consumption is still rising. GS reviews geo-engineering cooling technologies that mimic volcanic eruptions and strong ocean winds by raising Earth's albedo, and views them as a future climate-management tool, not a substitute for de-carbonization.

Europe Oil Services: GS's Top Projects analysis shows an accelerating LNG investment cycle, partly catalysed by disruption through the Strait of Hormuz. It identifies c.280 mtpa of capacity reaching FID across 2025-30, up c.52 mtpa or 23% from c.228 mtpa in TP2026. GTT is the preferred exposure and Technip Energies is cut to Neutral.

ASML Wilton site visit: GS lists five takeaways: strong momentum on High NA and its ecosystem, a deep competitive moat, multiple avenues for output optimisation, strong momentum in installed base management and upgrades, and Match Act concerns that GS views as overdone. GS reiterates Buy (on Conviction List).

Airtel Mobile Commerce (Airtel Money): GS initiates at Neutral. The platform operates across 13 markets in East and Francophone Africa, and GS expects a revenue ex-FX CAGR of c.26% over FY26-31E, driven by penetration of Airtel Africa's subscriber base and rising ARPU.

Europe hardware read-across from Nvidia's 3QFY27 results: GS sees ASML as best positioned in its coverage given exposure to leading-edge Logic and Memory, a stronger moat and longer lead times. ASMI, BESI and TPRO should benefit from rising process complexity and from advanced packaging and testing requirements, respectively.

Tencent 3Q26: revenue grew 8% y/y and operating profit fell 6% y/y, 2ppts and 6ppts below GSe on softer international games and elevated AI spending. GS cuts 4Q26E/FY27E/FY28E adjusted net profit by 5%/11%/11%. Concerns are record capex and compute prepayments driving FCF outflow, slower core top-line and profit growth, and rising investment in new AI products. GS rates Tencent Buy.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy (on Conviction List) after the Wilton site visit, citing High NA momentum, a deep moat and installed base upgrades. GS views Match Act concerns as overdone.
GS cuts Technip Energies to Neutral and prefers GTT, as the LNG FID wave grows.
GS initiates Airtel Mobile Commerce at Neutral, expecting a revenue ex-FX CAGR of c.26% over FY26-31E.
GS keeps Buy on Tencent after a 3Q26 miss, with revenue +8% and operating profit -6% y/y. It cuts 4Q26E/FY27E/FY28E adjusted net profit by 5%/11%/11%.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees ASML as best positioned, with ASMI, BESI and TPRO benefiting from process complexity and advanced packaging and testing needs.
GS expects an acceleration in the LNG FID cycle. GTT is preferred and Technip Energies is cut to Neutral.

earnings_insights: Tencent 3Q26 (reported, GS first take): revenue +8% y/y and operating profit -6% y/y came in 2ppts and 6ppts below GSe, on softer international games and elevated AI spending. GS cuts 4Q26E/FY27E/FY28E adjusted net profit by 5%/11%/11%.
Nvidia 3QFY27 results (reported) are used by GS as a read-across for European AI-indexed names. The note gives no Nvidia figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The FOMC held the rate in October. 'Almost all' participants see further hikes as likely appropriate, so risk is tilted toward tightening.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed funds rate, size of next hike
macro_indicators.reading: 25bp, with 'a couple' of participants open to more than 25bp
macro_indicators.interpretation: A larger hike could be considered if incoming inflation data are 'unfavorable'.
GS's Carbonomics note says the current emission path is more likely to reach this range than the 1.5-2°C goal.

risk_factors: Governance, environmental and execution risks of geo-engineering
Tencent: record capex and compute prepayments driving FCF outflow, and a slowdown in core business growth
geopolitical: Disruption through the Strait of Hormuz has increased the focus on LNG supply security and diversification away from geopolitical chokepoints, and has helped catalyse the LNG investment cycle.
